chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Nuaym, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One of his sons complained [of illness] to him, so he said: 'O my son! Say.'
'O Allah! Heal me with Your healing, and cure me with Your cure, and grant me well-being from Your affliction, for I am Your servant and the son of Your servant.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for healing from illness in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a concise yet profound formula for seeking cure, highlighting the theological balance between divine agency and human humility. By invoking Allah's specific attributes of healing and medicine, the supplicant acknowledges their status as a servant, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on direct reliance on the Divine during times of affliction. This dua serves as a practical spiritual tool for believers to maintain faith and patience while undergoing physical trials.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Nuaym, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘One of his<sup>asws</sup> sons complained to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son! Say,

‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Heal me with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Healing, and Cure me with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Cure, and Grant me good health from Your<sup>azwj</sup> affliction, for I am Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant and son of Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant’’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al- Husayn ibn Nu’aym from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Once one of the sons of Imam (a.s.) complained from an ailment and he told him to say, ‘
O Lord, cure me with Your treatment, provide me medication from Your medicine and relieve me from Your misfortune; I am Your servant, son of Your servant.’”
